summary: Rajan Gurukkal is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Calicut (~1970–1972). He served as Director of the School of Social Sciences at Mahatma Gandhi University (~1996–2008) and held a post at the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru (~2010–2015).

Rajendra Chandra Hazra was an Indologist who completed doctoral studies under Sushil Kumar De (~1932–1936). He held posts at Jagannath University (1931), the University of Dhaka (1939–1949), and Sanskrit College and University (1951–1972).

Rajendralal Mitra was an Indologist, historian, archaeologist, and linguist. He studied at the Hindu School (~1837–1839) and the University of Calcutta, and served as president of the Asiatic Society around 1885.

Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist who studied at Presidency University, Kolkata (~1903–1907) and the University of Calcutta (~1905–1907). He held posts at Calcutta (~1908–1911), Presidency University, and Banaras Hindu University (~1928–1930).

Ralf Kramer is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Hamburg (~1991–1997) under David P. Jackson (~1992–1997) and at the University of London (~1994–1995). Around 2002, he was Aris Librarian for Tibetan & Himalayan Studies at the Bodleian Libraries.

Ralph Abraham was a philosopher who studied at the University of Michigan (~1954–1960) and under Debabrata SenSharma. He held posts at UC Berkeley (~1961–1962), Columbia University (~1962–1964), and UC Santa Cruz (attested 2009).

Ralph Lilley Turner was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Christ's College, Cambridge (~1907–1912). He held a post at Banaras Hindu University (~1920–1922) and served as Director of SOAS University of London (~1937–1957).

Ralph T. H. Griffith was an Indologist who studied at The Queen's College (~1843–1847) and under Horace Hayman Wilson (~1845–1849). He succeeded James R. Ballantyne and served as Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1883).

Ram Karan Sharma was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Patna University (~1946–1953) and UC Berkeley (~1957–1959) under Murray Barnson Emeneau, later holding posts at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University (~1953–1961) and the Central Sanskrit Board (attested 1981).
Ram Mohan Roy was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He founded the Brahmo Samaj and established Presidency University, Kolkata, in 1816.

Ram Niwas Pandey is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and Pt. Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, completing his doctorate under Hit Narayan Jha.

Ram Shankar Tripathi was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1971–1994) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1989–1998).

Ram Sharan Sharma was a historian and Indologist who studied at Patna College, Patna University, and SOAS. He held posts at Patna College (~1943–1973), SOAS, the University of Toronto (~1965–1966), and the University of Delhi (~1973–1985).
Rama Nath Sharma is a linguist and Indologist. He served as a professor at the University of Rochester (~1968–1976) and held a professorship at the University of Hawaii beginning around 1976.

Ramaprasad Chanda was a historian and Indologist educated at Dhaka College and Scottish Church College. He held positions at Rajshahi Collegiate School, the University of Calcutta, and as Superintendent of the Archæological Section at the Indian Museum (1921–1931).
Ramaranjan Mukherji was an Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta from roughly 1944 to 1953. He later held an academic post at the University of Calcutta from around 1956 to 1970.
Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indologist. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at L. D. Arts College (attested 1938) and as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat Vidyapith.

Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar was an Indologist who studied at the University of Mumbai and Heidelberg University. He held posts at Fergusson College, served as Secretary at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1939–1994), and was Director at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1949–1974).

Ramesh Chandra Majumdar was a historian and Indologist who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, among other institutions. He held posts at the University of Calcutta (~1914–1921), the History of Bengal Publication Committee, and the University of Chicago (~1958).

Ramesh Shankar Gupte was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. In 1967, he was attested as department head at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and as a visiting lecturer at Wake Forest University, Salem College, and Winston-Salem State University.
